candidate_sentence_map.S1: AS LHV Group delivered its strongest financial performance to date in 2024, despite Estonia remaining in recession, declining interest rates and intensified competition for loans and deposits.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Consolidated net income increased 11% to EUR 338.3 million, supported by 8% growth in net interest income to EUR 273.3 million and a 24% increase in net fee and commission income to EUR 60.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: Pre-tax profit rose to EUR 175.1 million, while net profit increased 7% to a record EUR 150.3 million, including EUR 149.0 million attributable to the owners of the parent.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Basic earnings per share increased to EUR 0.46 from EUR 0.44.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Growth in operating volumes was substantial.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Total assets increased 23% to EUR 8.7 billion, net loans rose 28% to EUR 4.6 billion, and customer deposits grew 21% to EUR 6.9 billion.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Corporate and retail lending in Estonia each increased by approximately 21%, while the UK SME loan portfolio expanded 338% to EUR 348 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: The loan portfolio remained of generally strong quality, although the Group increased expected credit losses to EUR 16.3 million from EUR 11.5 million as the economic outlook weakened and some corporate and consumer exposures deteriorated.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Operating expenses rose 14% to EUR 146.9 million, mainly because of higher employee numbers and investment in the UK retail bank.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: As a result, the cost-to-income ratio increased slightly to 43.4% from 42.3%, while return on equity declined to 24.5% from 29.0%.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: LHV Pank remained the main earnings contributor, generating EUR 140.5 million of net profit, down 1% year on year as higher income was offset by 12% growth in expenses, increased credit losses and deposit repricing.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: LHV Bank increased net income to EUR 44.6 million and net profit to EUR 5.8 million, while launching retail banking and achieving independent funding through rapid deposit growth.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: LHV Kindlustus reached a second profitable year, with gross written premiums up 21% to EUR 38.0 million and net profit increasing to EUR 1.2 million from EUR 0.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Asset management income was broadly stable, although profit declined to EUR 1.6 million because no performance fee was earned.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Paytech’s net profit increased 40% to EUR 0.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Capital and liquidity remained strong despite balance-sheet expansion.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: The CET1 ratio was 16.89% and total capital adequacy was 20.68%, while the LCR and NSFR stood at 187.5% and 154.4%, respectively.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: The Group issued EUR 300 million of MREL-eligible bonds and EUR 20 million of Tier 2 bonds, while redeeming EUR 20 million of Additional Tier 1 bonds.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: The share price fell 7% to EUR 3.245.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Management proposed a 2024 dividend of EUR 0.09 per share, compared with EUR 0.13 paid during 2024 for the prior year.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: For 2025, LHV expects slower growth and lower profits as interest rates decline, but plans continued loan expansion and more efficient operations.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: K1, K2, K3, K6, K7, K8 and K9 are PRESENT with supporting sentences identified. K4 (Assets under management) and K5 (Customer base growth) are MISSING - no mention of AUM growth, market share in pension system, or specific customer numbers for LHV Pank/LHV Kindlustus. The summary captures most HIGH-priority information and key MEDIUM elements except these two. The overall picture is captured but with notable omissions of medium importance, justifying a 'Generally yes' (score 3).
